title: Power bank: safe teardown
summary: A power bank holds one or more lithium cells (round 18650s or flat pouches) and a small board that charges them from USB and boosts them to 5 V. Both are worth keeping. Open the case with plastic tools only, never pushed in where they can reach a cell, and cut the cell leads one at a time.

steps.text: Check it first, before you charge it or open it. Look for a swollen or split case, heat while it is idle, rattling, scorch marks or a sweet chemical smell. If you see any of these, stop and follow safety_swollen_lithium: store it whole and do not open it. If it looks sound, charge it on concrete or a metal tray where you can watch it, then use it to charge a phone: a working power bank is worth more whole. Read the model number on the label: the Anker PowerCore 10000, model A1263, was recalled for fire risk (the recall covers units with listed serial numbers; if you cannot check, treat any A1263 as recalled).
steps.warn: Don't charge or use a swollen, hot, damaged or recalled pack. Retire it as in safety_swollen_lithium.

steps.text: If it works, run it down: use it to charge something until its lowest light blinks or it stops. A half-empty pack releases less energy if a cell is damaged.

Set up outdoors, or on concrete, stone or a metal tray, away from anything that burns, with a bucket of dry sand and a metal tin close by. You need old plastic cards, small screwdrivers (for screws only), side cutters, pliers, tape, a meter, a hair dryer and safety glasses. Take off rings and watches.
Look for screws first, under the label, rubber feet or the end caps, and take them out.

Open the case at the end with the USB ports, where the board usually sits, not along the middle over the cells. Cells are often just behind that end too, so follow the seam and go in only as far as you must. If it is glued or taped, warm the seam gently with a hair dryer, then work a plastic card or pick into the seam and along it a little at a time. If the shell is welded shut with no screw or seam, leave the bank whole.
steps.warn: Use plastic only. Never push a blade, screwdriver or pry bar into the case: cells sit close behind the end cap too. Keep the case under about 54 °C (130 °F). A stab into a cell can start a fire.

steps.text: Slide the insides out or lift the cover. Look at the cells at once: if any is puffed, dented, wet, crusty, hot or smells sweet, stop and follow safety_swollen_lithium without cutting or bending anything. Before you cut anything, note how the cells are joined: side by side with both ends strapped together (parallel), or end to end (series). Take a photo or draw it.
Undo the screws holding the board, so the wires don't tear when the cells move.
Cut the leads between the board and the cells one at a time, close to the board. Tape each cut end before you cut the next.
steps.warn: Never cut two wires in one bite of the cutters. That shorts the cells through the blades.

steps.text: Free the cells from the case. If they are stuck down with glue tape, warm the outside of the case under them and lift with a plastic card. Lift pouch cells evenly from one end.
steps.warn: Never bend a pouch cell or lever a cell out with metal. If it won't come, add gentle warmth, under about 54 °C (130 °F), and wait.

steps.text: Leave round cells that are joined in parallel as one block: they already sit at the same voltage. If you need them apart, peel the nickel strip off with pliers, as in teardown_laptop_battery, and keep the pliers from touching both ends of one cell or two cells at once. Do not dent or bend the cell tops. Never pull the tabs off a pouch cell.
Measure each cell or block with the meter on DC volts and write the reading on it. Above 3.0 V: good. 2.0–3.0 V: charge gently and watch it. Below 2.0 V: reject. Then follow test_lithium_cell.

Test the board: connect its own cells, or healthy cells wired the same way (the same number in series), to its battery pads, matching the + and − marks. Plug a USB charger into its input: the lights should show charging. Then switch it on and measure about 5 V at its USB output.
steps.warn: Check polarity twice: a backwards cell can destroy the board and heat the cell. Do this on a metal tray of sand where you can watch, and unplug at once if a cell gets warm.

steps.text: On magnetic wireless power banks, ease the ring of magnets and the flat charging coil out of the front panel with a plastic tool.
steps.warn: Keep magnets away from pacemakers and small children.

steps.text: Store healthy cells with their ends taped, part charged (about 3.7–3.8 V), in a metal tin or a box of dry sand with the lid loose, somewhere cool and away from where people sleep. Keep any damaged cell in its own tin of sand outdoors (safety_swollen_lithium).

notes:
## What's worth keeping and why

- **The whole power bank, if it works.** Charges phones, radios, lights and LoRa nodes, and recharges from any USB charger or solar USB panel.
- **Cells.** Round 18650 cells or flat pouch cells, about 3.7 V each. Teardowns found two 18650s rated 3.7 V, 2,600 mAh in an Anker Astro E1, a single 18650 in a lipstick-size bank, and two flat 5,000 mAh cells wired in parallel in an Anker Astro E3 (DigiKey USB batteries). Cells joined in parallel sit at the same voltage: keep the block whole and treat it as one big cell. Build them into packs for lights and radios (build_18650_pack).
- **Charge-and-boost board.** Charges the cells from USB and boosts them to 5 V USB. Some boards also protect the cells; others leave that to a separate protection board. Give it a healthy cell and you have a power bank again. Newer boards do all of this with one chip, such as the INJOINIC IP5385 in the Anker A110Z (ChargerLAB Anker A110Z). Reuse a board only with the same number of cells in series that it came with.
- **Protection board (BMS).** Some banks have a separate small board on the cells. In the A110Z it holds a protection chip, two MOSFETs and a temperature sensor (ChargerLAB Anker A110Z). Keep it with its cells.
- **Magnets and coil.** Magnetic wireless banks carry a ring of magnets in the front panel and a coil of fine stranded (Litz) wire (ChargerLAB Anker A110Z).

## Variations

- **Taped end cap:** the Xiaomi Mi Power Bank 10400 has its top cover on double-sided tape; under it, four screws free the cells and board, which slide out together. The battery is soldered to the board (iFixit Mi 10400).
- **Glued clamshell:** the Xiaomi Mi Wireless Power Bank Essential (WPB15ZM) is glued hard at the sides; iFixit heated it and slid a thin, stiff tool, a card or a screwdriver, along the seam; use plastic only. Three screws hold the board, and two glue tapes hold the battery; iFixit warms it and pries it up, but ease a cell only with a plastic card and no force (iFixit Mi Wireless).
- **Snap-fit, cells in series:** the Anker A110Z's front panel snaps off. Its two cells are in series, joined by spot-welded nickel strip, with grey heat-conducting compound packed round the board (ChargerLAB Anker A110Z).
- **Large banks:** the Xtorm XB304 appears to hold 18650 cells four in series and two in parallel, with its boards glued in at the USB end and a double-walled case (iFixit Xtorm XB304).
- **Recalled packs:** about 1,158,000 Anker A1263 units (those with listed serial numbers) sold in the US from June 2016 to December 2022 were recalled after 19 reports of fires and explosions. CPSC says to stop using them and not to put them in rubbish or curbside recycling (CPSC Anker A1263).

## Lithium safety

- Dropping, crushing and puncturing damage lithium cells, and so does heat above about 54 °C (130 °F). Damaged cells belong in a fire-resistant container with sand (OSHA SHIB 06-20-2019).
- Some burning lithium cells can give off hydrofluoric acid, whose effect on skin may not be felt for hours (OSHA SHIB 06-20-2019). Stay upwind.
- Cover terminals with electrical tape and never put lithium batteries in household rubbish or recycling bins (EPA lithium-ion batteries). Never bend or short a cell, and keep spares part-charged in a metal box away from where people sleep (safety_swollen_lithium).

## What to leave

- **Recalled packs, and any cell that is swollen, dented, leaking, hot or below 2.0 V.** Tape and store them in sand (safety_swollen_lithium).
- **Foam, heat-spreading film and potting compound.**
- **Display screens and their small controller chips** in digital-display models.

## Testing what you got out

- **Cells:** voltage first, then capacity and self-discharge (test_lithium_cell).
- **Board:** as in the board step.
